reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and replaces five inline midpoint copies with one helper, but builds a new getExpectedAmount next to the existing getScheduledAmount instead of extending it.

duplication.why: The inline copies are gone, but getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount now both carry the missing/number/range dispatch, only one of them knowing about approximate amounts.

placement.why: Amount rules live in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is derived in api-models' toExternal, where the tree maps entities to API shapes.

scope.why: Changes are limited to schedule amount rules, the API model field, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Two parallel entry points for 'the amount a schedule is expected at' will drift; the API's expectedAmount already ignores the approximate rule because it goes through the op-less helper.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount with getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount) instead of getExpectedAmount(_amount, _amountOp), so it skips the approximate-amount rule that the other server paths apply.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts: getExpectedAmount re-implements getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch under a new name (with an added op branch) instead of one function delegating to the other.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch; api-models toExternal (and the client's getScheduledAmount callers) go through the op-less getScheduledAmount instead.
